newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: U.N. to open human rights office in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to open human rights office in Colombia.

text.p: Colombia's government on Friday signed an agreement with the United Nations allowing it to operate a human rights watchdog office in Bogota for at least 17 months.
The agreement, a copy of which was made available in Bogota, was signed in Geneva by Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia and Jose Ayala-Lasso, the U.N. high commissioner for human rights.

The main aim of the six-member U.N. office, which will be given sweeping powers to inspect detention facilities and war zones across Colombia, was to advise authorities on "the promotion and protection of human rights," the agreement said.
But the agreement stressed that this should be done "within the context of the violence and internal armed struggle the country is living through."
Colombia has been fighting a low-intensity war with leftist guerrillas seeking to overthrow the state since the mid-1960s.

Gunmen of the left and right have killed with impunity throughout the country for decades and human rights groups claim that the country's dreaded right-wing paramilitary groups, or death squads, operate with the complicity or tacit support of the military.

Under terms of the accord, the U.N. rights office has been authorised to monitor the situation in Colombia for the next 17 months. The accord can be renewed for a one-year period after the initial 17 months expires, but it can be renounced by either party at any time.
